Explore our campus in-person or from the comfort of your own home!
ISKL’s rigorous international curriculum combines academic excellence with holistic development, preparing students for global success through comprehensive internal and external assessments.

ISKL's co-curricular programs in academics, arts, athletics, and community service empower students to pursue their passions, fostering global awareness and citizenship in a culturally diverse environment.
Our holistic support system fosters academic and social-emotional growth through a collaborative, evidence-based approach, ensuring our students are equipped to fulfill their potential.
Joining ISKL means becoming part of a vibrant community celebrating diversity and nurturing international mindedness, with over 60 nationalities enriching our shared experiences and perspectives.

In the heart of Kuala Lumpur, ISKL's 25-acre campus is a hub of advanced learning. State-of-the-art technology and innovations provide a world-class learning environment where students can discover their passions and shape their path as global citizens.

ISKL is a non-profit school whose revenue from tuition is reinvested to recruit and retain the best international educators and enhance the school environment, ensuring the best possible learning experience for our students.
Every child learns differently and our aim is to provide students with the opportunities, experiences, and pathways that best suit their abilities, interests, and aspirations.

Our approach to teaching and learning is based on a Learning Principles framework that acts as a guide for both our students and teachers. In addition to ensuring a robust academic program, they reflect our focus on social and emotional learning and our belief in the importance of student voice and choice in their own learning.

pages.title: ISKL Guiding Statements - The International School of Kuala Lumpur
blocks: At ISKL, we are committed to preparing students for a future where happiness, fulfillment, and adaptability are key. We believe in equipping them with the skills to thrive in an ever-changing world, fostering resilience, and the ability to learn, unlearn, and relearn.
Our Guiding Statements and Strategic Plan, informed by global best practices, research, and the input of our community, build on our past and present to lead us into the future.
We aim to continue pushing the boundaries as a global leader in education. Join us on this journey as we work together toward achieving our Vision and Mission.

We are dedicated to preparing students for a vibrant, fulfilling life by nurturing both academic excellence and personal growth. To us, success means fostering social and emotional well-being, building meaningful relationships, enjoying fulfilling careers and lives, and making a positive impact on the world.

Every day, we empower students by giving them a voice and choice in their learning journey. We help them discover their passions, develop essential skills, and make ethical contributions to society. This commitment lies at the heart of our vision of success for students.
Know yourself, care for all, and create a better world.
We are an inclusive and dynamic community where passions, values, and competencies are cultivated to inspire learners to shape their path as global citizens.

Our Values are central to our school’s culture and guide the beliefs, attitudes, and behaviors that we expect of ourselves and each other. They apply equally to our students, faculty, staff, and community members.
Our School-Wide Learning Results (SLRs) are based on six learning outcomes that are embedded within our curriculum and culture to ensure students have the skills they need to succeed in the future.

ISKL’s Strategic Plan 2026–2030 sets the direction for our school over the next four years. Shaped by extensive research, global best practice, and consultation with students, parents, employees, alumni, and the Board, it remains firmly grounded in our Mission, Vision, and Values.

Its four Strategic Priorities, Living Our Values, Inspiring Our Learners, Advancing Our Systems, and Designing Our Future, will guide how we support our students’ well-being, create future-ready learning experiences, strengthen specialized pathways, and prepare our students and school for the future.

pages.title: About Us - The International School of Kuala Lumpur (ISKL)
blocks: Since 1965, The International School of Kuala Lumpur (ISKL) has been a center of excellence in international education.

ISKL is a co-educational, private, non-profit school responsible for the learning journey of over 1,700 students aged 3-18, representing over 60 nationalities, at its campus in the heart of Kuala Lumpur.

ISKL offers a robust international curriculum which combines leading North American educational frameworks with global best practice. The curriculum recognizes that students are on a lifelong learning journey and is driven by ISKL’s purpose to prepare our students for life itself. ISKL is the longest-running IB World School in Malaysia and has been authorized by the International Baccalaureate Organization to provide the prestigious International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP) since 1989.

ISKL is also the only school in Malaysia to offer this range of high-quality, transdisciplinary pathways in High School that enable every learner to choose the curriculum best suited to their abilities, interests, and aspirations. Options available include PRAXIS (for Grade 9 students), the full IBDP, the Global Impact Diploma (available in 2027-2028) and ISKL's High School Diploma. This flexibility creates global further education opportunities with ISKL’s students receiving acceptances from leading universities worldwide.
ISKL is accredited internationally through the Council of International Schools (CIS) and in the United States through the Western Association of Schools and Colleges (WASC).
Across its divisions, ISKL strongly focuses on service and sustainability and is a member of the Eco-Schools organization and the Green Schools Alliance.

ISKL believes in the power of open and ongoing communication between parents and teachers, recognizing its critical role in supporting children's success. This communication not only strengthens the bond between parents and teachers but also actively involves parents in their children's educational journey, promoting their social-emotional well-being.

Throughout the year, we maintain frequent communication with parents to keep them informed about their child's progress. Student work is shared via online education-specific platforms, or through materials sent home. Assessments are regularly provided to showcase students' growth towards grade-level expectations, fostering a transparent and collaborative environment.

ISKL believes in a strong partnership between home and school , scheduled conferences and individual appointments with teachers, counselors, and school staff offer personalized support and help to quickly address any concerns related to the students' learning and well-being.

Our counseling team, library, teaching and learning departments, parent association, and administration collaborate to provide parent education sessions, enriching the educational experience of every child at ISKL. Parents are encouraged to actively participate in classroom activities as volunteers, guest readers, and resource speakers, further enhancing the learning journey of our students.
Since 1965, our international school has been a beacon of learning and growth, cultivating a community where students thrive, and global citizens are formed.
Explore our history timeline to see how our values have shaped generations of learners and leaders dedicated to making a difference,
ISKL’s humble origin begins in an old palace on Jalan Maxwell in the Kenny Hills area, built in the 1920s by the Sultan of Selangor.
Under our first Head of School, Robert Fendley, classes began in September 1965 with 48 students, and numbers grew rapidly, doubling anticipated enrollment in its first year.

When the Malaysian government acquired the site, The Society for The International School of Kuala Lumpur was granted a 2.6-hectare parcel of land in Jalan Kerja Ayer Lama, Ampang Jaya. Learning at the new premises commenced in 1976.
In 1992, the Melawati campus opened to accommodate the Elementary School, and the Ampang campus became the home of the Middle and High School.
In March 1995, the High School moved to a new wing of the Ampang campus.

For more than a quarter of a century, ISKL was split into two geographically separate campuses. With a continued increase in enrollment, ISKL began searching for a site to accommodate growth, reunite both campuses and create a unique, student-centered learning environment.
After an extensive search, the 26-acre site on Ampang Hilir was selected, and in April 2016, the groundbreaking ceremony took place.
Construction was completed in time for the commencement of the 2018-2019 academic year and in August 2018, ISKL opened its doors at the Ampang Hilir Campus to over 1,700 students.
After 27 years apart, all three school divisions were reunited on one campus.

ISKL began with a modest start in 1965 in Istana Tetamu on Jalan Maxwell, following several months of planning by the first head of school, Robert Fendley, Dr. Luebke of the Office of Overseas Schools, and school board members.
There were nine teachers and 48 students in Grades 6 to 9, and the academic courses were based on an American curriculum.
When Al Chudler arrived in 1968, he inherited a school where enrollment was rapidly increasing due to the influx of oil companies investing in Malaysia.

The fine arts and athletics programs were thriving and the first inter-school debates and sports activities were organized with Singapore American School. This marked the beginning of a friendly rivalry that continues to this day.
By the end of this decade there were nearly 400 students from 24 countries enrolled at ISKL.
